body:
# Problem

If an autocommand handler focuses the tab page we're closing during a `:tabonly` (with some conditions), we hit an assert failure in `win_close_othertab()`

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/31de0d69fc745b342352f04a03cbcb90211c4edc/src/nvim/window.c#L3162-L3165

For this to occur, we need:
- `nvim_buf_delete()` to trigger [`close_windows()`] (as is done in [`cmdwin.lua`'s `_cleanup()`])
- `close_windows()` then calls `win_close_othertab()`, unlinking the window (indirectly via [`win_free_mem()`])
- then up the call tree in `tabpage_close_other()`, the loop continues (we don't detect `tp_lastwin == wp` since we've unlinked the window)
  https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/510f61555b9da5800ccd13de2336c90a64c0b9a5/src/nvim/ex_docmd.c#L5323-L5337
- so the loop assumes that `curtab != tp`, and continues

but we've refocused `curtab` so the `ex_win_close()` call passes `tp` as `curtab`, causing the assert to fail

# Solution

Handle this by detecting the focus of `curtab` and abort closing the tab.

[`close_windows()`]: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/510f61555b9da5800ccd13de2336c90a64c0b9a5/src/nvim/window.c#L2578
[`cmdwin.lua`'s `_cleanup()`]: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/510f61555b9da5800ccd13de2336c90a64c0b9a5/runtime/lua/vim/_core/cmdwin.lua#L134-L144
[`win_free_mem()`]: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/510f61555b9da5800ccd13de2336c90a64c0b9a5/src/nvim/window.c#L3321

comment_data.body: This is precautionary - happy to revert to the `assert()`
Revert to the assert. Actually I'd say the same assert should be added at the start of `ex_win_close()` as well.
alternatively we could check `got_int` (maybe that's already done somewhere inside of `ex_win_close` codepath?)
Interesting - I suppose `got_int` relies on the user detecting the infinite loop whereas this is a little more failsafe? Won't burn a CPU if the user's wandered off etc
yeah, i'm just thinking of what the common pattern is. this is fine for now.

comment_regular_data.body:
[Test failure](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/actions/runs/32842845744/job/97785940054?pr=41475) looks unrelated, rebasing

<details><summary>Test output</summary>

```
FAILED   .../work/neovim/neovim/test/functional/lua/comment_spec.lua @ 245: commenting toggle_lines() respects tree-sitter injections
Expected values to be equal.
Expected:
"    -- set background=light"
Actual:
"    \"set background=light"
stack traceback:
	.../work/neovim/neovim/test/functional/lua/comment_spec.lua:262: in function 'validate'
	.../work/neovim/neovim/test/functional/lua/comment_spec.lua:269: in function <.../work/neovim/neovim/test/functional/lua/comment_spec.lua:245>
```

</details>

AI findings


>  1. **`:tabonly` can close the wrong tab.** `ex_tabonly`'s guard `tp->tp_topframe != topframe`
>     re-reads the live `topframe` each pass, so an autocmd switching to a *third* tab makes it destroy
>     the tab that was current. Repro: 3 tabs, `:tabonly` from tab 3, `autocmd WinClosed * ++once`
>     calling `nvim_set_current_tabpage(tab2)` — only tab 2 survives. Capturing the keep-tabpage once
>     in `ex_tabonly` fixes it and subsumes the `tp == curtab` check added here.
>  
>  2. **Infinite loop in `tabpage_close()`**: `while (curwin->w_floating) { ex_win_close(forceit,
>     curwin, NULL); }`. `ex_win_close` returns void, so an early bail (`no_write_message()`,
>     `is_ctx_win()`, `window_layout_locked()`) leaves `curwin` unchanged and the loop never
>     terminates. Repro: `set nohidden`, `:tabnew`, float via `nvim_open_win` on a modified buffer with
>     `b_nwindows == 1`, then `:tabclose`. Pre-existing, and missing the 1000-iteration bound the
>     sibling loop has.
>  
>  3. **`tp->tp_lastwin == wp` compares a `wp` autocmds may have freed** — in this PR's own repro,
>     `nvim_buf_delete` inside WinClosed frees it via `close_windows()`. UB, plus a spurious "close
>     failed" if the allocator reuses the address. `win_valid_any_tab(wp)`, or comparing handles rather
>     than pointers, would be sound.
>  
>  4. **The new `tp == curtab` guard runs after `ex_win_close`**, but `trigger_tabclosedpre(tp)` runs
>     before it and can leave `curtab == tp` on its own: it restores `ptp` only `if
>     (valid_tabpage(ptp))`, else falls back to `first_tabpage`. If that is `tp`, the first iteration
>     trips the new assert. Moving the check to the top of the loop body covers both.
>  
>  5. **The abort is silent** — `:tabclose N` / `:tabonly` become a no-op with no message and no
>     `v:errmsg`, so scripts can't distinguish it from success.
>  
>  6. **The new test asserts only `assert_alive()`**, so it won't catch a regression that closes the
>     wrong tab. `tabpagenr('$') == 2`, `tabpagenr() == 1`, `#nvim_list_wins() == 2` would pin it. The
>     name also mentions `:tabclose`, but only `:tabonly` is exercised — `:tabclose N` is a separate
>     entry point into `tabpage_close_other`.
>  
>  7. The comment says the guard aborts "a `:tabonly`", but `tabpage_close_other` is also `:tabclose N`
>     (ex_docmd.c:5230) and mouse tabline close (mouse.c:160).
Sorry about the review-request @zeertzjq, had the browser page open and it hadn't loaded Justin's comment

> AI findings
> 
> 1. **`:tabonly` can close the wrong tab.** `ex_tabonly`'s guard `tp->tp_topframe != topframe`
>    re-reads the live `topframe` each pass, so an autocmd switching to a _third_ tab makes it destroy
>    the tab that was current. Repro: 3 tabs, `:tabonly` from tab 3, `autocmd WinClosed * ++once`
>    calling `nvim_set_current_tabpage(tab2)` — only tab 2 survives. Capturing the keep-tabpage once
>    in `ex_tabonly` fixes it and subsumes the `tp == curtab` check added here.

I think this is fine - we're ok with another tab being closed - if the autocmd changes the tab, then I'd say that's on it. The check here is to avoid crashes via asserts, rather than trying to patch up behaviour after an autocmd

> 2. **Infinite loop in `tabpage_close()`**: `while (curwin->w_floating) { ex_win_close(forceit, curwin, NULL); }`. `ex_win_close` returns void, so an early bail (`no_write_message()`,
>    `is_ctx_win()`, `window_layout_locked()`) leaves `curwin` unchanged and the loop never
>    terminates. Repro: `set nohidden`, `:tabnew`, float via `nvim_open_win` on a modified buffer with
>    `b_nwindows == 1`, then `:tabclose`. Pre-existing, and missing the 1000-iteration bound the
>    sibling loop has.

As mentioned, pre-existing but I've added the 1000-limit fix.

> 3. **`tp->tp_lastwin == wp` compares a `wp` autocmds may have freed** — in this PR's own repro,
>    `nvim_buf_delete` inside WinClosed frees it via `close_windows()`. UB, plus a spurious "close
>    failed" if the allocator reuses the address. `win_valid_any_tab(wp)`, or comparing handles rather
>    than pointers, would be sound.

This is well known UB, but vim has this regularly / it's pre-existing so I don't think it's relevant. The LLM is also wrong - `win_valid_any_tab` has the same UB. Or also, for example:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/fb083f3850c242e14613de517811a3818bef98db/src/nvim/buffer.c#L502-L503


> 4. **The new `tp == curtab` guard runs after `ex_win_close`**, but `trigger_tabclosedpre(tp)` runs
>    before it and can leave `curtab == tp` on its own: it restores `ptp` only `if (valid_tabpage(ptp))`, else falls back to `first_tabpage`. If that is `tp`, the first iteration
>    trips the new assert. Moving the check to the top of the loop body covers both.

Done

> 5. **The abort is silent** — `:tabclose N` / `:tabonly` become a no-op with no message and no
>    `v:errmsg`, so scripts can't distinguish it from success.

I think this is fine - we already just return early if an autocmd messes up global state

> 6. **The new test asserts only `assert_alive()`**, so it won't catch a regression that closes the
>    wrong tab. `tabpagenr('$') == 2`, `tabpagenr() == 1`, `#nvim_list_wins() == 2` would pin it. The
>    name also mentions `:tabclose`, but only `:tabonly` is exercised — `:tabclose N` is a separate
>    entry point into `tabpage_close_other`.

The test isn't about catching regressions, just that vim doesn't crash. Would you like me to modify the test still?

> 7. The comment says the guard aborts "a `:tabonly`", but `tabpage_close_other` is also `:tabclose N`
>    (ex_docmd.c:5230) and mouse tabline close (mouse.c:160).

I don't think that's helpful, it's a comment. I've changed the comment to note that `:tabonly` is an example, rather than mentioning all possible callers of the function (and presumably keeping the comment updated as the callers change!)
